'''Teena Meredith Gerhardt''' (born 1980){{r|loc}} is a professor of mathematics at [[Michigan State University]]. Her research focuses on [[algebraic topology]], including [[algebraic K-theory]] and [[equivariant stable homotopy theory]].{{r|msu}}

==Education and career==
Gerhardt studied mathematics as an undergraduate at [[Stanford University]], graduating in 2002. She completed her Ph.D. in 2007 at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]].{{r|cv}} Her dissertation, ''The <math>R(S^1)</math>-graded equivariant homotopy of <math>\operatorname{THH}(\mathbb{F}_p)</math>'', was supervised by [[Lars Hesselholt]]; it concerned the [[homotopy theory]] of the [[Topological Hochschild homology|topological Hochschild homology ring]] of a [[finite field]].{{r|mg}}

She was a Zorn Postdoctoral Fellow at [[Indiana University]] from 2007 until 2010, when she joined Michigan State University as an assistant professor. She was promoted to associate professor in 2017 and full professor in 2023.{{r|cv}}

==Recognition==
Gerhardt has won multiple teaching awards at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology and Michigan State University.{{r|cv}} She was elected as a [[Fellow of the American Mathematical Society]] in the 2025 class of fellows.{{r|fams}} She was named as a Fellow of the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]], in the 2027 class of fellows, "for her work ranging from local involvement with her AWM Student Chapter to her large-scale national service".{{r|fawm}}
